(expanded letters in italics: um, æt)”.

div.head: I Cn 18.3
div.ab: Forþam God ælmihtig us ealle geworhte ⁊ eft deopum ceape gebohte, þæt is mid his agenum life, þe he for us eallum sealde.
Forðan Gód ælmihtig us ealle geworhte ⁊ eft deopum ceape gebohte, þæt is mid his agenum blode, ðe hé for us eallum ageat.
Forþam God ealmigtig us ealle geworhte ⁊ eft deapum ceapum gebohte, þæt is mid his agenan life, þe he for us sealde.
quoniam Deus omnipotens nos omnes creauit et iterum caro precio redemit, id est propria uita, quam ille pro nobis tribuit. (Cons. Cn.)
quoniam Deus omnipotens nos omnes creauit et iterum caro precio redemit, id est propria uita, quam ille pro nobis tribuit.
Forþan Gód ælmihtig us ealle geworhte ⁊ eft deopum ceape gebohte, þæt is mid his agenum blode ðe hé for us eallum ageat.
Forþam God ælmihtig us ealle geworhte and eft deopum ceape gebohte, þæt is mid his agenum life, þe he for us eallum sealde.
Denn Gott der Allmächtige hat uns alle erschaffen und nachher mit hohem Preise(n A) erkauft, nämlich mit seinem eigenen Leben (Blute B), das er für uns alle hingab (vergoss B).
For God Almighty created us all and afterwards bought us at a high price (prices, A), namely with his own life (blood, B), which he gave (shed, B) for us all.
For God Almighty made us all, and afterwards bought us at a great price, namely, with his own blood which he shed for us all.
For God almighty created us all and afterward paid a high cost for us, namely, his own life which he gave for us all.
div.note: O here gives the Consiliatio Cnuti (Quadripartitus has no separate 18.3). Liebermann compares VI Atr 42.2, 9; Apoc. 5:9.; Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G; BR: added from Gesetze I p. 301, October 2026 (MS Cons)

note.seg: Vgl. Gl Christus 1. 3. ‘Blut’ (statt ‘Leben’), wie hier B, liest u. II 3 Inst
Cf. Gl Christus 1. 3. ‘Blood’ (instead of ‘life’), as here in B, is also the reading of II 3 Inst below
